headline: A 2022 Senate bill that would have expanded voting access, changed redistricting rules, and set new election and campaign finance rules, but the Senate never voted on it.
what_it_does: If adopted, this bill would have made voter registration easier, including automatic and same-day registration, and would have expanded options like vote-by-mail and early voting. It would have limited removing people from voter rolls and made Election Day a federal holiday. It would have created a new federal crime for corruptly interfering with someone registering to vote or helping others register, and would have required states to conduct post-election audits for federal elections. It also would have set redistricting criteria, generally barred mid-decade redistricting, expanded the ban on foreign campaign spending, and changed which places must get federal preapproval before changing voting rules.

who_it_affects.how: They would have had easier ways to register and vote, such as automatic registration, same-day registration, vote-by-mail, and early voting.
They would have had stronger protections against being removed from voter registration lists.
Election Day would have become a federal holiday, giving federal employees a paid day off.
They would have had to follow new registration, voting access, post-election audit, and redistricting requirements.
They would have faced an expanded ban on foreign campaign spending and an alternative campaign funding system for certain federal offices.

who_it_affects.group: People who help others register to vote
who_it_affects.how: They would have been protected by a new federal crime aimed at people who corruptly interfere with voter registration help.

who_it_affects.group: States and localities with past voting restrictions
who_it_affects.how: Changes to their voting practices would have required federal preapproval under new criteria for which places are covered.
The bill would have included provisions to improve voting access on tribal lands.
